sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Compare Fourier series formulas for intervals } (0,2\pi), (-\pi,\pi), \text{ and } (0,2l).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} x^2 dx = \frac{8\pi^2}{3}\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} x^2 \cos nx dx = \frac{4}{n^2}\)

(2 Mark)

\(b_n = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} x^2 \sin nx dx = -\frac{4\pi}{n}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } x^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{3} + 4\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\cos nx}{n^2} - 4\pi\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\sin nx}{n}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Given } f(x) = x^2 \text{ in } (0,2\pi), \text{ find Fourier series.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Constant term written as } \frac{a_0}{2} \text{ for consistency with } a_n \text{ formula when } n=0\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_c^{c+2\pi} f(x) dx \text{ (same formula as } a_n \text{ with } n=0)\)

(3 Mark)

\(\text{Then } \frac{a_0}{2} = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_c^{c+2\pi} f(x) dx, \text{ which is average value of } f(x)\)

(3 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Explain why constant term is } \frac{a_0}{2} \text{ instead of } a_0.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{If } f(x+2\pi) = f(x), \text{ Fourier series remains same}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Coefficients computed over any interval of length } 2\pi \text{ are same}\)

(3 Mark)

\(\text{Series represents periodic extension of function defined in basic interval}\)

(3 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{What happens to Fourier series if function is shifted by period?}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} [\int_0^{\pi} 1 dx + \int_{\pi}^{2\pi} 2 dx] = 3\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{1}{\pi} [\int_0^{\pi} \cos nx dx + 2\int_{\pi}^{2\pi} \cos nx dx] = 0\)

(2 Mark)

\(b_n = \frac{1}{\pi} [\int_0^{\pi} \sin nx dx + 2\int_{\pi}^{2\pi} \sin nx dx] = \frac{2}{n\pi}[1-(-1)^n]\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } f(x) = \frac{3}{2} + \frac{2}{\pi}\sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{\sin nx}{n}\)

(2 Mark)
